title: Practitioner Exam
description: REPLACE: frame the exam - how many questions, rough time, retake policy. Author questions by hand here or generate + review them in the Question Bank app, then export its exam.json over this file. REPLACE the xx- id prefix with a short token for THIS course (di, ct, 2hr...) and keep the rest of the shape: every id is <token>-m<module>-q<question>, where m is the module's place in the course's reading order and q the question's place in it. Ids must be unique across every course, numbers are never reused, and npm run verify fails any other shape. Every question needs a `bloom`: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze or Evaluate. State it rather than leaving it out - an absent bloom is read as Understand, which will misreport the exam. Weight the pool to Apply and above, and cap Remember: an exam that asks what things are called does not measure whether anyone can do the job.

questions.scenario: REPLACE: the situation the candidate is in. A question without one is usually a definition in disguise.
questions.prompt: REPLACE: put the candidate in a situation and ask what they would do. Apply is the workhorse level - most questions should sit here or above.
questions.explanation: REPLACE: teach, don't just judge - why the answer is right.
questions.source: REPLACE: where the course covers this (shown only in results)

questions.scenario: REPLACE: the situation. Name a workshop by its title if you must refer to one - never 'Lab 3, step 4'.
questions.prompt: REPLACE: a multi-select stem - phrase as 'select all that apply'. Analyze asks what follows from a situation, not what a thing is called.
questions.explanation: REPLACE: multi-select questions are graded all-or-nothing.

questions.scenario: REPLACE: a proposal a reasonable colleague might make, which is wrong here for a reason the scenario states.
questions.prompt: REPLACE: Evaluate gives two defensible options and asks which is better on a stated criterion. Hardest to write, and what separates a senior exam from a quiz.
